content.title: About
content.content: Fatty fish are species that contain a high level of omega‑3 polyunsaturated fatty acids such as EPA and DHA. Examples include salmon, mackerel, herring, sardines and trout. They have a rich flavor, firm texture and are valued for their beneficial fats, protein, vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Omega‑3s from fatty fish support heart and brain health.
Wild salmon gets its pink color from a diet rich in crustaceans and krill.
Herring has been traditionally preserved by pickling, smoking and canning in northern cuisines.
Mackerel migrates long distances, traveling thousands of kilometers each year.
In Japan, saba (yellowtail) is traditionally eaten during New Year celebrations.

items.title: Rich source of omega‑3
items.content: EPA and DHA help maintain cardiovascular health, reduce inflammation and support brain development.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Fatty fish provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, B6 and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides selenium, iodine and potassium, essential for thyroid function and fluid balance.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: One of the few natural food sources of vitamin D, which supports bone health.

items.title: Mercury contamination
items.content: Some larger predatory fish may contain higher mercury levels; pregnant women and children should limit intake.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals with fish allergy can experience reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium in smoked products
items.content: Smoked or salted fish can be high in sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: People with pancreatitis or gallstones may experience discomfort after eating fatty fish.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fatty fish can be baked, grilled, steamed or enjoyed as canned. It pairs well with lemon, herbs, olive oil and vegetables. For a lighter preparation, it can be marinated in yogurt or soy sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh fish in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen fish should be kept at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Use airtight packaging and keep away from strong odors.

oatmeal-regular-or-quick-made-with-milk-.title: Oatmeal, regular or quick, made with milk, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Oatmeal is made from whole oat grains that can be rolled (regular) or finely cut (quick‑cooking). When prepared with milk and added fat, it becomes creamy and richer in flavor. Oatmeal is commonly enjoyed as a hearty breakfast or as a base for sweet and savory dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats have been cultivated for over 5,000 years and are one of the oldest grain crops.
Rolled, steel‑cut, and instant oats differ in particle size, which determines cooking time.
Cooking with milk boosts calcium and vitamin D content compared with water.
Adding fat (butter, oil, cream) improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins and makes the dish more satiating.
Oats contain beta‑glucan, a soluble fiber that helps lower cholesterol.

items.title: Rich in beta‑glucan
items.content: Beta‑glucan helps reduce LDL cholesterol and supports immune function.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides sustained energy and helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, pantothenic acid, and folate aid metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D from milk
items.content: Preparing with milk increases calcium and vitamin D, essential for bone health.

items.title: Beneficial fats when added
items.content: A modest amount of butter or plant oil enhances flavor and aids absorption of fat‑soluble nutrients.

items.title: Allergy to oats or milk
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to oat proteins or milk proteins and should avoid the product.

items.title: Higher calorie content with added fat
items.content: Fat increases the energy density, so portion size should be monitored, especially on weight‑control diets.

items.title: Presence of phytic acid
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or thorough cooking lowers its level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook oatmeal in milk, add a pinch of salt and a small amount of butter or oil. Top with fruit, berries, nuts, honey, or spices such as cinnamon and vanilla. Quick‑cooking oats are convenient in the microwave, while regular rolled oats need 5‑10 minutes of simmering.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry oats in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked oatmeal should be cooled and kept in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Potato salad is a classic dish made from boiled potatoes, often combined with eggs, pickles, onions, herbs, and dressed with mayonnaise or sour cream. Variations may include ham, sausage, seafood, or additional vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato salad is popular in Russia, the CIS, and the United States, where it is a staple at picnics and barbecues.
The first recorded potato salad recipes date back to the 19th century, after potatoes became widely available in Europe.
Regional versions differ: Russian recipes often add pickles, while U.S. versions may include bacon and green onions.
It is commonly prepared ahead of time, as the flavors meld together over several hours.
Traditional recipes use mayonnaise, but modern twists incorporate yogurt, mustard, or olive oil.

items.title: Carbohydrate source
items.content: Potatoes provide a quick source of energy through complex carbohydrates.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The salad retains B6 and folate, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and heart function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: If the potato skins are left on, the salad adds dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Protein from add‑ins
items.content: Eggs, meat, or legumes in the salad boost its protein content.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Mayonnaise and sour cream make the salad calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Pickles and prepared dressings can raise sodium, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Eggs commonly used in the salad can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Bacterial growth
items.content: If left at room temperature for more than 2 hours, the salad can become a breeding ground for bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Potato salad is served chilled as a side dish or a standalone meal. It can be eaten with a fork, spoon, or as a sandwich filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Allow the salad to reach room temperature before serving for optimal flavor.

rice-white-with-carrots-fat-added.title: White Rice with Carrots, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: A ready‑to‑eat product consisting of boiled white rice mixed with finely diced carrots and added vegetable fat. It is commonly used in baby foods and in diets that require higher energy density.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice provides quickly digestible carbohydrates, making it a good energy base.
Carrots add beta‑carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.
The added fat increases caloric content and helps absorb fat‑soluble vitamins.
Traditionally used in infant nutrition for babies from 6 months old.
When stored properly, the product remains fresh for up to 12 months.

items.title: Rapid energy source
items.content: White rice is quickly converted to glucose, delivering fast‑acting energy for active children and athletes.

items.title: Supports vision
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots converts to vitamin A, essential for eye health and immunity.

items.title: Improved vitamin absorption
items.content: Added vegetable fat enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Well‑cooked rice and soft carrots make the product gentle on the stomach, suitable for infants and those with digestive issues.

items.title: Balanced macronutrients
items.content: The combination of carbs, a modest amount of fat, and some protein provides sustained satiety.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice has a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid blood sugar spikes in people with diabetes.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to the specific vegetable oil used.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Rice can contain trace amounts of arsenic; a varied diet is recommended.

items.title: Potential over‑consumption
items.content: Due to its high calorie density, portion control is important, especially for children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a standalone dish, add to soups, stews, or use as a side for meat and fish. It reheats well in the microwave or on the stovetop, stirring to prevent sticking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. After opening, use within 3‑4 days, or store in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks for longer shelf life.

content.title: About
content.content: Diet iced black tea in a bottle is a refreshing beverage made from selected black tea leaves, extracted, filtered and carbonated. The sugar‑free version is sweetened with artificial sweeteners, making it low‑calorie.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black tea is rich in polyphenols that may support cardiovascular health.
Carbonated versions are often perceived as more refreshing in hot weather.
Diet drinks commonly use stevia or sucralose as sweeteners.
PET bottles preserve flavor and aroma longer than glass at room temperature.
The first commercial iced tea appeared in Japan in the early 20th century.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Polyphenols in black tea help combat free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports concentration
items.content: Caffeine in black tea improves alertness and cognitive performance without a sharp energy spike.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: The diet version contains less than 5 kcal per 100 ml, suitable for weight management.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: A water‑based tea beverage contributes to daily fluid intake.

items.title: No added sugar
items.content: Absence of sugar helps maintain stable blood glucose levels.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Certain people may experience discomfort from sucralose or stevia.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: Gas can cause bloating in those with a sensitive stomach.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine can amplify the effects of stimulants and reduce the efficacy of sedatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chill the bottle and sip slowly. Add a lemon wedge or mint for extra aroma if desired. Do not heat the carbonated drink, as it will lose its fizz.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 3‑5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Yogurt with almond milk is a blended beverage that mixes traditional dairy yogurt with plant‑based almond milk. It has a smooth, creamy taste with a subtle nutty note and a velvety texture. Suitable as a stand‑alone snack or as a base for smoothies, desserts, and breakfasts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The combination delivers a double dose of probiotics from the yogurt and plant nutrients from the almond milk.
Almond milk is lower in calories and fat than cow’s milk while retaining a pleasant nutty aroma.
Yogurt‑almond milk drinks are often fortified with vitamin D and calcium to support bone health.
The product is popular among vegetarians and those with lactose intolerance because part of the dairy is replaced with a plant component.
In some countries it is served frozen as a “yogurt ice‑cream cocktail.”

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Yogurt provides live bacterial cultures that support gut health and the immune system.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The blend offers a good source of complete protein, essential for muscle and tissue maintenance.

items.title: Vitamin E
items.content: Almond milk is rich in vitamin E, a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Yogurt is a calcium source, and almond milk is often fortified, together promoting strong bones.

items.title: Reduced lactose
items.content: Lowering the proportion of dairy reduces lactose content, making it more suitable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to cow’s milk may still react to the yogurt component, even with almond milk added.

items.title: Tree‑nut allergy
items.content: Almond milk contains nut proteins that can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Flavored versions may contain added sugars; choose unsweetened options if blood‑glucose control is a concern.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While almond milk is low‑calorie, the yogurt base adds calories; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink it straight, blend into smoothies, pour over granola, stir into oatmeal, create parfaits, or freeze for a creamy ice‑cream alternative.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 1‑4 °C. After opening, consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may separate.
